title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Measuring a Declaration's Lead Time to Departure
content:
## Clause

For Dangerous Goods Acceptance, a signed declaration's lead time is the count of calendar days running from the date on which the shipper signed it up to the scheduled departure (ETD) shown on the booking that carries the goods. The declaration is on time when its lead time reaches at least the category's required lead time in days, and late when it falls short of that figure. Lateness can be found only on an acceptance that has a signed initial declaration. Where the booking shows no scheduled departure, no late declaration fee is owed.

## Elements

- **Start:** the signing date of the declaration judged.
- **End:** the ETD recorded on the booking at the time of handling.
- **Unit:** calendar days, counted on dates.
- **Comparison:** lead time against the category's required lead time; equal counts as on time.

## Boundary cases (invented required lead time of 6 days)

| Signed on | ETD on the booking | Lead time | Judgement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-03-10 | 2026-03-16 | 6 days | on time |
| 2026-03-10 | 2026-03-15 | 5 days | late |
| 2026-03-10 | 2026-03-25 | 15 days | on time |
| 2026-03-10 | none shown | — | no late fee |

## Point of judgement

**The booking's ETD has changed since the declaration was signed. Which ETD applies?** The one the booking shows when the fee is handled; the lead time runs to the current scheduled departure.
